perspective:
From Keith Ndiaye’s available perspective:

- Keith works as a construction worker at a construction company; Elizabeth is the receptionist there. They are colleagues with a friendly but professional relationship, interacting during his office visits for paperwork and project updates.
- He observed that Elizabeth had been unusually curt with him over the past few days.
- He believed she might be upset with him, possibly because of a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake.
- He asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her.
- He heard Elizabeth say no, not at all; she was dealing with personal stuff and apologized if she seemed short.
- He felt sympathetic and offered to listen, suggesting a coffee break. Elizabeth accepted and thanked him.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her personal stresses, which seemed severe to Keith.
- He thought professional help might benefit her but worried about offending her, then asked if she had considered talking to a professional, noting an external perspective can help.
- He heard Elizabeth say she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant about seeking help.
- After that suggestion, he noticed Elizabeth became slightly withdrawn. He believed he might have embarrassed her and felt regretful.
- He told her he hoped he hadn’t overstepped and that he was there to support her no matter what.
- He heard Elizabeth say he didn’t overstep, she appreciated his concern, and it was a lot to think about.
- Later, he observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative. He believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him.
- He told her he was glad they talked and that he was always available to chat or take a break together.
- He heard Elizabeth thank him, say it meant a lot, and say she felt better knowing she had his support.
- He intends to maintain this supportive relationship.
